summary: Repository predates Go modules; add go.mod so it builds and tests in module mode.
base_test_status_reason: There is no go.mod at base_sha, so the module-mode step `go test ./...` cannot run before the change (the GOPATH-mode first step passes at base on the repository's own tests).

provenance.note: Evaluator-only. base_sha is the parent of the upstream commit that added go.mod; that commit is never reachable from the sealed clone.
provenance.fail_mode_note: Replaced the build-mode fixture in M4-04. With no go.mod at base nothing compiles in module mode, so the hidden test (which shells out to `go list -m`, `go env GOMOD`, `go list ./...` and `go build ./...` with GO111MODULE=on) is first run in GOPATH mode where it compiles and fails on assertions. Prompt unchanged.

test_command_note: Step 1 runs the root package in GOPATH mode (GO111MODULE=off; still supported by Go 1.27 but deprecated) so the held-out test compiles without a go.mod and fails on its assertions (`go list -m` in module mode errors). Step 2 is the real acceptance check in module mode. If a future Go release drops GOPATH mode, revert this fixture to fail_mode build with test_command `go test ./...`.

reference.note: Evaluator-only. The verifier renders the reference patch from upstream: git diff --binary -M base_sha commit -- paths, per step.
